import math
from fractions import Fraction

# Path: M 95,40 A 27,27 0 1,0 41,40 A 27,27 0 1,0 95,40
p0 = (95, 40); p1 = (41, 40); r = 27
rx = ry = r

d = math.hypot(p0[0]-p1[0], p0[1]-p1[1])
print("chord length:", d, "diameter:", 2*r)

# Chord == diameter -> center is uniquely the midpoint (radius correction not needed)
cx = Fraction(p0[0]+p1[0], 2); cy = Fraction(p0[1]+p1[1], 2)
print("center:", cx, cy)
print("dist center to endpoints:", math.hypot(p0[0]-cx, p0[1]-cy), math.hypot(p1[0]-cx, p1[1]-cy))

def arc_points(start_ang, end_ang, sweep, n=360):
    # sweep=1 -> angle increasing, sweep=0 -> angle decreasing (SVG y-down coordinates)
    a0 = start_ang
    a1 = end_ang
    if sweep == 1:
        while a1 < a0: a1 += 2*math.pi
    else:
        while a1 > a0: a1 -= 2*math.pi
    return [(float(cx)+r*math.cos(a0+(a1-a0)*i/n), float(cy)+r*math.sin(a0+(a1-a0)*i/n)) for i in range(n+1)]

a_start = math.atan2(p0[1]-cy, p0[0]-cx)  # 0
a_end = math.atan2(p1[1]-cy, p1[0]-cx)    # pi
arc1 = arc_points(a_start, a_end, 0)
arc2 = arc_points(a_end, a_start, 0)

# All points on circle radius 27
maxdev = max(abs(math.hypot(x-float(cx), y-float(cy))-r) for x, y in arc1+arc2)
print("max radial deviation:", maxdev)

# Arcs cover opposite halves -> full closed circle
side1 = {y < 40 + 1e-9 for x, y in arc1}
side2 = {y > 40 - 1e-9 for x, y in arc2}
print("arc1 on upper side (y<=40):", side1, "arc2 on lower side (y>=40):", side2)

# Angular coverage
span1 = abs(a_end - a_start)
print("angular span each arc (deg):", math.degrees(span1), "total:", 2*math.degrees(span1))

closed = arc2[-1] and math.hypot(arc2[-1][0]-p0[0], arc2[-1][1]-p0[1]) < 1e-9
full = abs(2*math.degrees(span1) - 360) < 1e-9
equal_radii = (rx == ry)
print("closed:", closed, "full 360:", full, "rx==ry:", equal_radii, "maxdev small:", maxdev < 1e-9)

if closed and full and equal_radii and maxdev < 1e-9 and side1 == {True} and side2 == {True}:
    print("Shape is a full circle (answer A; ellipse K would need rx != ry)")
    print("CHECK PASS")
else:
    print("CHECK FAIL")
